Correction methods have been developed to reduce these atmospheric signals, but they do not generally perform well on smaller\u2010scale studies of volcanoes. To address this, we have developed a novel atmospheric mitigation method termed LiCSAtmo that uses independent component analysis (ICA) to identify atmospheric signal patterns and subtract them from the time series. By using ICA, we are able to empirically estimate the spatial pattern and temporal behavior of atmospheric noise signals with no constraints other than that they are non\u2010Gaussian and statistically independent of other signals (such as deformation). Furthermore, as our algorithm can work in both space or time, we can mitigate a variety of signals that may not be non\u2010Gaussian and independent of other signals in one domain by working in the other. We applied our algorithm to Vesuvius, where displacement of up to  mm\/year is highly correlated with topography, and successfully corrected the apparent seasonal reversal of the long\u2010term subsidence caused by atmosphere. In a comparison with Global Navigation Satellite System\u2010derived measurements of deformation, our approach dramatically outperforms a state\u2010of\u2010the\u2010art correction method based on a weather model, reducing root\u2010mean\u2010square error by  (0.006\u00a0m vs. 0.017\u00a0m).
